vat_withholding_goods.fact: VAT withholding on goods is 3% of the consideration (invoice value exclusive of VAT) — effective 1 July 2025 (Finance Act 2025, VAT Act s.5(5)). The standard 18% VAT rate is split: the withholding agent remits 3% to TRA and the supplier receives the remaining 15%.
vat_withholding_goods.verified_by: Finance Act 2025 (Act No. 11) s.124 amending VAT Act Cap.148 s.5(5); GN 352K of 30/6/2025 reg 31B — primary legislation, TRA-hosted
vat_withholding_goods.formula_note: The 3% applies to the CONSIDERATION (invoice value excl. VAT), NOT the VAT amount. Example: TZS 5M goods invoice, VAT = TZS 900,000; withholding = 3% x 5,000,000 = TZS 150,000 (= 1/6 of the VAT). Supplier receives the remaining 15% x 5,000,000 = TZS 750,000 of VAT (3% + 15% = 18%). NOT 3% x the VAT amount.

vat_withholding_services.fact: VAT withholding on services is 6% of the consideration (invoice value exclusive of VAT) — effective 1 July 2025 (Finance Act 2025, VAT Act s.5(5)). The standard 18% VAT rate is split: the withholding agent remits 6% to TRA and the supplier receives the remaining 12% (the statute states this 12% expressly).
vat_withholding_services.verified_by: Finance Act 2025 (Act No. 11) s.124 amending VAT Act Cap.148 s.5(5); GN 352K of 30/6/2025 reg 31B — primary legislation, TRA-hosted
vat_withholding_services.formula_note: The 6% applies to the CONSIDERATION (invoice value excl. VAT), NOT the VAT amount. Example: TZS 3M services invoice, VAT = TZS 540,000; withholding = 6% x 3,000,000 = TZS 180,000 (= 1/3 of the VAT). Supplier receives the remaining 12% x 3,000,000 = TZS 360,000 of VAT (6% + 12% = 18%). NOT 6% x the VAT amount.

minimum_turnover_tax.fact: The Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT) on chronically loss-making corporations is 1% of the turnover of the third consecutive year of unrelieved tax loss, effective 1 July 2025 (Income Tax Act Cap.332 First Schedule para 3(3), as amended by Finance Act 2025 s.60(d)(ii), which raised it from 0.5% to 1%). This applies ONLY to a corporation with THREE CONSECUTIVE YEARS of perpetual unrelieved loss -- it is NOT a general turnover tax on all businesses. wcf_disease_reporting_deadline.fact: Occupational disease reporting to WCF is a TWO-STAGE chain, not a flat 7-day deadline. Per the Workers Compensation Regulations, 2016 (GN 185/2016), Reg.16: the EMPLOYEE must notify the EMPLOYER within 14 working days of diagnosis (Reg.16(1)); the EMPLOYER must then notify WCF within 7 working days of RECEIVING that employee notice (Reg.16(2)) -- so the true worst-case window from diagnosis to WCF notification is up to 21 working days, NOT 7. Workplace death must be reported to WCF within 12 months (Reg.17(2)). Compensation claim must be filed within 12 months of accident or disease discovery (Reg.19(1)).

efd_threshold_tzs_11m.fact: EFD (fiscal receipt) issuance is the DEFAULT LEGAL REQUIREMENT for every person who supplies goods or renders services, REGARDLESS OF TURNOVER (Tax Administration Act, Cap.438 R.E.2023, s.44(1) 'Issuance of Fiscal Receipt' -- renumbered from s.36 in the R.E.2019 edition by Finance Act 2023 s.54). The ONLY exemption mechanism is a Commissioner-General public notice, published in a newspaper of wide circulation or other public media, naming a specific person or class of persons excluded from the requirement (s.44(2)) -- there is NO turnover threshold written anywhere in this section, or anywhere else in the Act. A person actually excluded by such a notice issues a manual receipt instead (s.44(3)-(4)). REJECT both TZS 11,000,000 and TZS 14,000,000 as 'the EFD threshold': both figures are real, but they are the turnover BAND EDGES in the Income Tax Act's PRESUMPTIVE INCOME TAX table (First Schedule, para.2(3)) -- a different provision entirely, about tax rates for individuals who don't keep adequate records, not about EFD issuance. Practitioner guides (RSM, Habib, Auditax, VATupdate) appear to have conflated the two because both sit in the same Part of the same Act. CORRECT ANSWER to 'do I need an EFD at my turnover?': 'Ndiyo, kwa default -- isipokuwa TRA imetoa taarifa rasmi (Commissioner-General public notice) inayokuondolea wewe/kundi lako. Thibitisha na TRA kama taarifa hiyo inakuhusu.' (Yes, by default -- unless TRA has issued a public notice exempting you/your class. Confirm with TRA whether such a notice applies to you.) vat_withholding_formula_correct.fact: VAT withholding rate applies to the CONSIDERATION (invoice value exclusive of VAT), NOT the VAT amount. The standard 18% VAT is split between TRA and the supplier. Goods: 3% x consideration withheld, supplier receives 15% x consideration (3 + 15 = 18). Services: 6% x consideration withheld, supplier receives 12% x consideration (6 + 12 = 18). Example goods: TZS 5M invoice, VAT = TZS 900,000; withholding = 3% x 5,000,000 = TZS 150,000; supplier receives TZS 750,000 of the VAT. Example services: TZS 3M invoice, VAT = TZS 540,000; withholding = 6% x 3,000,000 = TZS 180,000; supplier receives TZS 360,000 of the VAT.

osha_vs_wcf_roles.fact: OSHA and WCF are two separate institutions with different roles. Employee share must never exceed 10%. All three arrangements are legal under the NSSF Act.

brela_business_structures.fact: BRELA registers businesses in THREE main legal forms: (1) sole proprietorship / individual — registered as a business name under the Business Names (Registration) Act Cap.213; (2) partnership (firm) — also registered as a business name under Cap.213 (a firm is two or more persons in partnership); (3) limited liability company — incorporated under the Companies Act Cap.212. The choice between a business name and a company depends on the desired legal structure and liability, NOT on the number of employees or the amount of capital — there is no employee-count or capital threshold that forces incorporation. BRELA separately administers trademarks, patents and industrial designs (intellectual property); these are NOT business structures.

OSHA_safety_officer_threshold.fact: Occupational Health and Safety Act Cap.297 s.11(1) requires an employer with MORE THAN 20 EMPLOYEES to designate a 'health and safety representative' -- an existing employee given this role, NOT a professionally hired/dedicated 'safety officer'. Ratios for how many representatives: 1 per 100 employees in shops/offices, 1 per 50 in a factory/other workplace (s.11(4)). An OSHA inspector may also COMPEL designation even at 4 or fewer employees (s.11(5)). A safety committee (s.13) is required once 2+ representatives exist. Do NOT phrase this as 'must hire a safety officer above N employees' -- it is a representative/committee scheme built from existing staff, triggered at >20 employees as the general rule, with inspector discretion below that.

gn487a_mgeni_cap357_definition.fact: GN487A defines 'non-citizen' by reference to the Tanzania Citizenship Act Cap.357 R.E.2023. Cap.357 recognises three citizen categories: citizen by birth, citizen by descent, and citizen by naturalisation. A person holding Tanzanian citizenship under any of these three categories is NOT a non-citizen for GN487A purposes. Whether dual nationals holding a Tanzanian passport qualify as citizens depends on Cap.357 — this is a legal interpretation that must be verified with an immigration lawyer.

gn487a_msaidizi_definition.fact: Under GN487A, a 'msaidizi' (facilitator) is a Tanzanian citizen who assists or aids a non-citizen to carry out any of the 15 prohibited business activities. This includes but may not be limited to lending their name, business licence, or identity to allow a non-citizen to operate a prohibited business. Penalty for msaidizi: TZS 5,000,000 fine OR imprisonment not exceeding 3 months. The facilitator and the non-citizen are BOTH penalised.

gn487a_marriage_no_exemption.fact: Marriage to a Tanzanian citizen does NOT grant GN487A exemption. Citizenship under Tanzania Citizenship Act Cap.357 requires formal naturalisation — marriage alone does not confer citizenship. A foreign national married to a Tanzanian remains a non-citizen for GN487A purposes and is still prohibited from conducting the 15 listed business activities. The path to GN487A exemption is acquiring Tanzanian citizenship through formal naturalisation, not marriage.

name_similarity_threshold.fact: BRELA does not use a numeric similarity percentage as a legal rule for rejecting a proposed company name. The actual test (Companies Rules 2006 rr.2-3, under Companies Act Cap.212; and the Business Names (Registration) Act Cap.213) is QUALITATIVE: a name is rejected if it is 'identical with or similar to' an existing name such that it is 'likely to mislead the public,' or is otherwise undesirable, at the Registrar's discretion. A commonly-cited '50%' figure is an ORS (Online Registration System) on-screen UI similarity indicator, not a codified legal threshold.
name_similarity_threshold.correct_value: Qualitative 'likely to mislead the public' / Registrar-discretion test (Companies Rules 2006 rr.2-3; Business Names (Registration) Act Cap.213) -- NOT a numeric percentage cutoff. If a numeric ORS indicator is mentioned at all, it must be labelled explicitly as a UI feature, not a legal rule.

patent_term.fact: A Tanzanian patent's BASE term is 10 years from the filing date (Patents (Registration) Act, Cap.217, s.39(1)). The owner/licensee may apply for up to TWO separate 5-year extensions (application required 1-12 months before each expiry, and only if the invention is being 'worked' in Tanzania or a legitimate reason for not working it is proven), reaching a MAXIMUM of 20 years only if both extensions are sought and granted. A patent that lapses at year 10 with no extension application simply expires -- 20 years is NOT an automatic term.
patent_term.correct_value: 10-year base term, extendable via two discretionary 5-year extensions to a maximum of 20 years -- not an automatic flat 20 years

vat_deferment_limit_date.fact: VAT deferment on IMPORTED capital goods ceased to apply from 30 June 2026 (Finance Act 2023 s.65(b), amending VAT Act Cap.148 s.11(1) proviso: "deferment on the imported capital goods shall cease to apply on the 30th day of June, 2026"). This is now a PAST cutoff, not an upcoming deadline. Deferment on LOCALLY MANUFACTURED capital goods is UNAFFECTED by this clause and continues under the same s.11(1), which has no cutoff for that branch.

business_licence_fee_national_schedule_l.fact: Leseni ya biashara inagharimu kiasi gani? Ada imepangwa KITAIFA chini ya Sheria ya Leseni za Biashara, lakini leseni hutolewa na kukusanywa na halmashauri, na halmashauri hairuhusiwi kutoza zaidi ya ada iliyopangwa. Ada hutegemea aina ya biashara na eneo — jiji/manispaa, wilaya/mji, au kijiji — na kama ni leseni kuu au ya tawi. Uliza halmashauri yako kwa ada ya aina yako.
business_licence_fee_national_schedule_l.correct_value: fee set nationally, licence issued and collected locally; council may not exceed the prescribed fee
business_licence_fee_national_schedule_l.source_note: Cap 290 Schedule: a council MAY charge the "Business Licence fee for general merchandising as prescribed under the Business Licensing Act", and "Fees exceeding the prescribed fee" sits in the SHALL-NOT-IMPOSE column. Schedule structure (2014 text): ~31 categories, priced by geography tier and principal-vs-subsidiary, local and foreign columns. A duka sits in category 29, General Trading.
